subquestions.text: Which MCP servers lead for general coding, repo, docs and browser verification work?
subquestions.evidence: official repo/docs, maintenance activity, coverage of the edit-test loop

subquestions.text: Which MCP servers and skills lead for frontend design, UI polish and unslopping?
subquestions.evidence: official docs, skill source, whether they close the screenshot-and-fix loop

What selection and security criteria distinguish safe, high-leverage MCP tools from token-hungry or risky ones?

claims.statement: GitHub's official MCP server covers repository reads, issues, pull requests, CI/CD workflow intelligence, and code/security findings.
claims.quote: Repository Management: Browse and query code, search files, analyze commits, and understand project structure across any repository you have access to.

claims.statement: Playwright MCP drives pages through structured accessibility snapshots rather than screenshots, but Microsoft's own docs say CLI+skills are more token-efficient for coding agents and MCP fits persistent, exploratory loops.
claims.quote: CLI: Modern coding agents increasingly favor CLI–based workflows exposed as SKILLs over MCP because CLI invocations are more token-efficient

claims.statement: Context7 supplies version-specific library documentation and code examples, and ships both a CLI+skill mode and an MCP mode.
claims.quote: Context7 pulls up-to-date, version-specific documentation and code examples straight from the source

claims.statement: Chrome DevTools MCP adds performance traces, network/console inspection, screenshots, and reliable browser automation to a coding agent.
claims.quote: Get performance insights: Uses Chrome DevTools to record traces and extract actionable performance insights.

claims.statement: Chrome DevTools MCP collects usage statistics by default and can send trace URLs to Google's CrUX API unless explicitly disabled.
claims.quote: Data collection is enabled by default. You can opt-out by passing the --no-usage-statistics flag

claims.statement: Sentry's MCP service is explicitly scoped to human-in-the-loop coding and debugging workflows, not general Sentry administration.
claims.quote: Sentry's MCP service is primarily designed for human-in-the-loop coding agents.

claims.statement: shadcn MCP lets an agent browse, search, and install components from public, private, or third-party registries using the project's components.json.
claims.quote: Browse Components - List all available components, blocks, and templates from any configured registry

claims.statement: Figma MCP extracts design context and can reuse real components via Code Connect, but Starter/View/Collab seats are limited to six tool calls per month.
claims.quote: Users on the Starter plan or with View or Collab seats on paid plans will be limited to up to 6 tool calls per month.

claims.statement: Anthropic's frontend-design skill is an anti-template design lead: it names generated-design tells and forces a token/plan review before code.
claims.quote: For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits

claims.statement: The frontend-design skill's second pass checks the plan against the brief and revises any part that would be the generic default before writing code.
claims.quote: Then review that plan against the brief before building

claims.statement: Supabase's official MCP server supports read-only and feature-scoped URLs that exclude mutating tools.
claims.quote: readOnly: When true, excludes mutating tools

claims.statement: Neon's MCP server is intended for local development and IDE integrations and is explicitly not recommended for production.
claims.quote: The Neon MCP Server is intended for local development and IDE integrations only. We do not recommend using the Neon MCP Server in production environments.

claims.statement: Postgres MCP Pro provides index tuning, EXPLAIN analysis, schema intelligence, and a restricted read-only mode for production.
claims.quote: Restricted Mode: Limits operations to read-only transactions and imposes constraints on resource utilization

claims.statement: The semgrep/mcp repository is deprecated and future MCP updates ship through the official semgrep binary; the server exposes security_check, semgrep_scan, custom-rule scans, and Semgrep AppSec findings.
claims.quote: This repository has been deprecated, and further updates to the Semgrep MCP server will be made via the official semgrep binary.

claims.statement: PortSwigger's Burp MCP extension is official, supports Streamable HTTP, SSE, and a stdio proxy, and asks for approval before sending HTTP requests or reading proxy history by default.
claims.quote: By default the extension asks for approval in Burp before sending HTTP requests or reading proxy history

claims.statement: OWASP's MCP Top 10 covers token mismanagement, scope creep, tool poisoning, supply-chain tampering, command injection, prompt injection, weak auth, missing audit, shadow servers, and context over-sharing.
claims.quote: MCP03:2025 - Tool Poisoning

claims.statement: OWASP classifies MCP tool poisoning as a top-10 risk, distinct from prompt injection via contextual payloads and from scope creep.
claims.quote: MCP02:2025 - Privilege Escalation via Scope Creep

claims.statement: Superpowers packages a software-development methodology — spec interrogation, implementation planning, red/green TDD, and subagent-driven development — as composable agent skills.
claims.quote: It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY.

claims.statement: Aqua's Trivy MCP plugin adds filesystem, container-image, and remote-repository vulnerability/misconfiguration scanning to an agent.
claims.quote: Filesystem scanning for local projects

claims.statement: Context7's library documentation is community-contributed, and the project disclaims guarantees of accuracy, completeness, or security.
claims.quote: Context7 projects are community-contributed and while we strive to maintain high quality, we cannot guarantee the accuracy, completeness, or security of all library documentation.
